# Testament of Dan — 7
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Cantabrigiensis) | **Section:** Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs

---

Dan's testament is about anger — specifically what anger does to a man's mind. He knew it from the inside. He had wanted to kill Joseph.

**1** He was 125 years old when he gathered his sons and said:

**2** In my whole life, I've learned one thing clearly: truth and patient dealing are good and pleasing to God. Lying and anger are evil. I know this because they almost destroyed me.

**3** I have to confess this to you: I wanted to kill Joseph. The spirit of jealousy told me: your father loves him more than you. One of Beliar's spirits put a sword in my mind and said: Take it. Kill him. Your father will love you when he's gone.

**4** The spirit of anger wanted me to tear Joseph apart like a leopard takes a kid. But God didn't let me find him alone. He protected Joseph from me. And he protected me from becoming a murderer.

**5** So listen, sons. Anger is blindness. When you're angry, you cannot see anyone clearly. Not your father. Not your mother. Not your brother. Not a prophet. Not a righteous man. Not a friend. They all look like enemies.

**6** That's what the spirit of anger does — it wraps a net around your eyes and fills them with hatred, so that you see every person as a threat to be destroyed.

**7** And once anger gets hold of a man's body, it takes over his soul too. The body does terrible things, and the soul signs off on them — because it can't see straight anymore.

**8** A powerful angry man is terrifying — he has his servants, his money to buy his way through, and his own physical strength. Even a weak angry man is twice as dangerous as he should be, because rage amplifies everything.

**9** This spirit runs alongside lying, at the right hand of Satan — they work together: cruelty and deception.

**10** Here's how anger works: it starts with words that provoke you. Then it strengthens itself through your reaction. Then it disturbs your mind with sharp losses. Then it drives you toward destruction.

**11** When someone speaks against you — don't be moved. When someone praises you — don't be moved either. Because here is the path: praise sharpens the mind, then an insult comes, and then the enraged man thinks his anger is righteous.

**12** If you lose something — property, reputation, something you love — don't spiral into rage. Beliar uses loss to hook into you. He takes away what you love so that you will be driven mad through grief. And from madness comes hatred. From hatred, enmity. From enmity, the desire for murder. From murder — death.

**13** So: see the trap ahead of time. Flee from lying. Love truth. Love patience.

**14** Tell your children what I'm telling you: the Savior of the nations is patient and humble and gentle. He teaches God's law not with words alone but through what he does.

**15** Walk away from everything unrighteous. Cling to God's righteousness. And your descendants will be saved.

**16** I know what will happen. In the last days you will depart from the Lord. You will stir up anger against Israel. You will be scattered. You will serve your enemies. But if you return to the LORD with all your heart — even from there, he will gather you back.

**17** When Beliar is finally destroyed, the LORD will save all who call on him. He will give eternal peace to all who trust in him.

**18** After Dan had said all this, he kissed his sons and died. They buried him in Hebron.

---
*End of Testament of Dan*
